title: Matt LaFleur: 'He's playing like an animal right now'
headline: Van Ness is 'playing like an animal' and Belton is expected at right tackle if healthy, while Banks's Thursday status remains open ahead of the Falcons game.
summary: LaFleur said the team is still determining availability for Thursday's game against Atlanta, and he would not commit on Aaron Banks until game time. He said Anthony Belton will be the right tackle if healthy and he expects him to play, though there are still about 48 hours to go. He praised Lukas Van Ness, saying Van Ness is impactful even when it doesn't show in the stat sheet and is 'playing like an animal right now.' He praised the linemen who protected Jordan Love on the end-zone hit, saying players need to have each other's backs even though the team has been penalized heavily. He called the 26 penalties through two games unacceptable, blaming pre-snap focus and two young players for the post-snap penalties. He said the defense improved on offsides, and the team will work on field position discipline. On the offense, he said the third-down struggles stem mostly from poor distances (third-and-ten too often), and the team needs more third-and-short situations. He defended Chris Brooks' red-zone carries as a function of the defense playing two high safeties, and he said the run game must be established. He called Skyy Moore's return work a big positive that gives the offense better field position, though the offense must capitalize on it. He said Jager Burton is a player he is excited about, but Aaron Banks has played well, so the left guard competition will play out. He also expects Burton to play meaningful snaps given the injuries, though he is also weighing continuity on the offensive line.

title: Sean McVay talks standout players in win over the Giants, competing with joy, Aaron Donald's impactful return & more
headline: Puka Nacua (groin/soft tissue) sat out Week 2 and is questionable for next week; Terrance Ferguson and Davante Adams earned strong praise.
summary: McVay said the Rams have no new serious injuries after the 28-6 win over the Giants, only some bumps and bruises, and that players were still trickling in. Puka Nacua had soreness in his groin area that got worse after a Thursday practice he got through, and he was ruled out even though the staff hoped he could play. Jordan Whittington also missed the game. McVay said he hopes Nacua plays next week, but he will not count on it and will decide based on how he feels in pregame warmups. He praised Terrance Ferguson as tough, smart, and a stud who showed resilience after a drop and then caught a touchdown, and he called Ferguson's versatility and run blocking valuable. Davante Adams had a strong week of preparation and got involved early, and McVay credited Matthew Stafford and the protection for the connections. On defense, McVay credited an attacking mindset, a sticky secondary led by Trent McDuffie, and pressure from both the front and the edges. Aaron Donald's return after roughly 1,000 days was emotional, and McVay said Donald still has rhythm and reps to regain. Wesley Bailey got his first career sack after Myles Garrett's absence opened up snaps for the group. McVay called special teams a clear area for improvement, citing field position issues despite a strong punt from the opposing punter. He said Blake Corum and Kyren Williams splitting carries is the ideal approach.

title: Coach John Harbaugh on latest with QB Jaxson Dart
headline: Dart's injury evaluation is still ongoing with no final decision; Harbaugh gave no timeline and expects Jameis Winston or the next man up to fill in if needed.
summary: Harbaugh declined to confirm or comment on reports about Jaxson Dart's injury, including reports that he could miss the season, saying evaluations are ongoing and no final decisions have been made. He said he will announce the direction when decisions are reached, and that he won't respond to every report. Harbaugh said Dart had an MRI and that doctors are consulting on the test results, but he would not describe the injury's severity or confirm whether it is worse than a sprained MCL. On Winston, he said he has absolute faith in every player on the roster and that whoever is next up would step in, mentioning Winston only as a good player who is there for a reason. Harbaugh said Dart was disappointed after the loss, and they discussed offense and the team's direction, but he would not say anything about the injury. He said the team's focus is on preparing for a range of possibilities and on the Tennessee Titans game in five days. He also said the team has lost quarterbacks many times and that backups have won games before, pointing to past playoff runs. He said the team is not playing close to its potential and needs to focus on playing its best as a whole.

title: Postgame Press Conference: Coach John Harbaugh on Jaxson Dart's status
headline: Jaxson Dart has an apparent sprained MCL with an MRI pending, Jameis Winston took over at QB, and Malik Nabers returned after an injury.
summary: Harbaugh said the Giants have a lot of work to do after the Week 2 loss to the Rams and will focus on becoming the team they need to be. Jaxson Dart's injury is in the neighborhood of a sprained MCL, but Harbaugh would not confirm details until an MRI the next day. He said the outcome is far less serious than the worst case, which he called good news. Jameis Winston came in at QB and, in Harbaugh's view, ran the offense well, but the team as a whole did not execute or make plays downfield. Brian Burns has a sprained ankle that Harbaugh described as low, and Andrew Thomas was also banged up late, with no clear status given. Harbaugh said Nabers' return was a positive development, and he dismissed the idea of a lull, blaming the lack of made plays. He also said the staff would second-guess its play calling, including the four straight runs from the 11-yard line after a recovered fumble, and that the interior of the Rams' pass rush was the biggest problem. The next game is in six days, and Harbaugh emphasized taking it one week at a time.
